text: Can the dynamical color matter on the Sigma(648) automaton be fermions in a dilute regime, and screen at every separation?
description:
OP-15: dynamical quarks as fermions.

Known: triplets that hop break the center (<Re P> = 0.0853 against 0.0005) and screen a static pair, but the matter is a classical color vector (the gauge-Higgs form), it condenses (0.998 of sites), no dilute regime exists at this bond scale, and the R = 3 screening gate fails by 3.02 standard errors against a gate of 3 (E-FRC-0138, E-FRC-0139).

Unknown: fermion matter on the automaton, a dilute regime, and the screening gate at half the box.

Why it matters: string breaking by dynamical quarks is a reproduction in R-FRC-0001 and not yet a measurement of the base.

Scope: a bond and mass grid, then larger boxes.

Skills: lattice gauge theory, fermion algorithms.

Where to start: test/experiment/gauge/finite-color-quarks.ts; test/experiment/gauge/finite-color-screening.ts.

The claims it would move: R-FRC-0006.

Evidence named: E-FRC-0138, E-FRC-0139.
